judged_text: The webhook endpoint gates only on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (i.e. CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET + CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY) while every consumer of the sync feature (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) additionally requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, leaving the two gates of the same feature out of sync. A self-hosted operator who sets the webhook secret and encryption key but no sync endpoint gets a live, writable credential-injection webhook while their own instance never participates in token refresh — credentials injected by the parent will sit and rot as tokens expire with no local refresh path, and the half-enabled state is invisible in .env.example's setup instructions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a configuration-gating mismatch: the new writable webhook `/api/webhook/app-credential` is enabled whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is truthy (defined as `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in `packages/lib/constants.ts`), and does not require `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (see `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`). By contrast, the new sync-related helpers `refreshOAuthTokens` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` only switch into “sync/parent-driven” behavior when both `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set. This can lead to an unintuitive partially-enabled configuration that isn’t clearly called out in `.env.example`. However, the finding’s claim that the instance then “never participates in token refresh” / has “no local refresh path” is not verifiable from the diff because `refreshOAuthTokens` explicitly falls back to the normal local refresh function when the sync endpoint is absent.
